risks: Case 1 needs the "not retired" sentence to carry a word for now (now, today, at present, presently, for now, at this time/stage/point, in this ticket). A faithful §5 that says only "not to be retired by an ACT" with no such word would fail, though the KPI's own wording says "now". Case 2 needs "fail(s) closed" or "by construction" in a sentence about retirement or old code, plus a later/future/follow-up/separate ticket or "(b)". Case 3 reads as a step any prose sentence that removes the module and carries no word that forbids it, defers it, makes it a condition or makes it history; gerund explanations ("removing the module lets…") and "removed, it would…" are excused. A code-block command that removes the module or its `.pth` always counts. The engineer writes §5 without seeing these readings, so the lead's acceptance run is the check.
lessons: For a scratch copy written by a shell redirect in this sandbox, use the sandbox's own temp folder; `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-112/td6/` is writable only through the file tool here. Printing only counts of found items in the driver keeps the implementation document unread while still showing why each case fails.
